topic:
The sharp global-treatment-effect frontier on random regular networks. For each integer n and d with nd even and 1<=d<n, G is drawn uniformly from the simple labeled d-regular graphs on [n], independently before the experiment and fully revealed. The asymptotic claim covers every admissible sequence d=d_n with d_n tending to infinity and d_n/sqrt(n) tending to zero. Constants in the risk equivalence are universal across such sequences. Probability of the asserted graph event tends to one along every such sequence. Exactly M(G,tau_GATE,2) in Kandiros-Harshaw-Savje (2026): fixed real potential-outcome schedules y_i(z) depend arbitrarily on z restricted to the closed neighborhood of i. Write y_i1=y_i(1^n) and y_i0=y_i(0^n). Require n^-1 sum_i y_ia^2<=1 for each a=0,1. No restrictions on irrelevant exposures, no bounded-degree interference order or additive response restriction. The schedule is fixed before treatment randomization; it may depend on the revealed graph. The experimenter selects any distribution D on {0,1}^n using G but no potential outcomes, then observes (Z,y(Z)). Estimators are all measurable functions of (G,Z,y(Z)); independent randomization is allowed. The minimax benchmark ranges over all such designs and estimators. tau_GATE(y)=n^-1 sum_i [y_i(1^n)-y_i(0^n)]. Risk R_2(G)=inf_(D,T) sup_(y in M(G,tau_GATE,2)) E_D[(T(G,Z,y(Z))-tau_GATE(y))^2], with any estimator randomization included. Determine an explicit evaluable deterministic scale r(n,d)>0, including every logarithmic factor, and prove universal 0<c<C<infinity such that P_G(c r(n,d)<=R_2(G)<=C r(n,d)) tends to one along every admissible d_n tending to infinity with d_n=o(sqrt(n)). The scale may not be defined as R_2 or as the original uncomputed minimax game. Whether it equals d/n, d^2/n, or an intermediate scale is answer-open. Give a total, implementable graph-dependent randomized design and estimator whose worst-case design MSE is at most C r(n,d) on the same high-probability graph event. Specify a finite sampling/evaluation algorithm and its time and memory cost; polynomial efficiency is desirable but not assumed as a second conjecture. If the computation is super-polynomial, supply an evaluable small-instance implementation and say so. Prove the lower bound against all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable estimators on the exact same published outcome class and revealed-graph experiment. A lower bound for CGD, cluster designs, linear estimators, or an assumed graph invariant does not suffice. A narrower hand-picked graph family, a risk bracket with a polynomial/log gap, an oracle estimator, or a positive result resting on an assumed lower certificate does not satisfy this kernel. Constants, designs, priors, truncation and proof mechanics are delegated. No requirement that one particular conjectured rate survive. This is an explicit same-framing retry of CausalSmith/doc/research/_bank/failed/exp_randomregular_fullgate_minimax_frontier_v1 (reraise_status: retry), not a new internal problem. The archived derivation proves a d^2/[n log(d+1)] all-procedure lower edge and d^2/n seed-design upper certificate. It does not solve the matched frontier. Three solve rounds stopped at a uniform Boolean radius-two operator/covariance bound. The new work must solve that bottleneck or derive a genuinely different attaining design or stronger all-procedure converse; reproducing the bracket is failure. External focused searches found no closure; active restricted-design topics are distinct. Consumer: Karrer et al., Network experimentation at scale (2020/2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08591, describes the deployed Facebook cluster-randomized framework for global treatment effects and two case studies. The theorem would give its global-rollout design question a sharp precision benchmark in the diffuse regular-network regime: how sample requirements grow with degree and whether an alternative design can improve over the current CGD d^2/n benchmark. Random regular graphs are a declared benchmark, not an assumption asserted about Facebook data. Eckles-Karrer-Ugander (JCI 2017), https://doi.org/10.1515/jci-2015-0021, studies the same global treatment contrast and design bias-variance tradeoff.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The archived attempt established only a logarithmic risk bracket. This presolve derives a new sparse-range radius-two collision tail on the uniform simple regular law and combines it with a published adjacency spectral bound. For the remaining denser range, an exact fourth-trace decomposition reduces the sufficient operator estimate to one signed four-distinct-vertex reachability moment, rather than an unbounded Boolean matrix expansion. Exhaustive enumeration of the 70 labeled cubic graphs on six vertices and 19,355 on eight vertices checks the rational probability identities and covariance algebra; these finite checks do not prove asymptotics. A separate deterministic covariance calculation supplies a weaker alternative certificate and identifies a necessary operator scale for this seed-estimator spine only.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform signed four-vertex moment bound in the original dense subrange, retaining cancellations, shared witnesses and residual-degree dependence; independently audit the displayed sparse switching proof and inherited lower and seed arguments.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact eight-vertex moment identity, then bound its signed five-probability combination by a four-root switching calculation. A failed sufficient moment route must be distinguished from failure of the full answer-open minimax problem; check the weaker covariance certificate before abandoning the design.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_randomregular_fullgate_minimax_frontier_matched_retry.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the constant-factor minimax MSE scale for the full GATE on uniform simple d-regular graphs, uniformly over every sequence d→∞ with d=o(√n), and attain it with a total one-shot graph-dependent design and measurable estimator on the exact unrestricted neighborhood-interference outcome class.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published anchor gives only d/n ≲ R₂(G) ≲ d²/n. The failed CausalSmith run improves the all-procedure lower edge to d²/[n log(d+1)] and supplies a legal seed-design upper certificate of order d²/n, but three solve rounds did not remove the remaining logarithm. Thus the true scale could equal either edge or an intermediate expression. Existing conflict-graph and cluster procedures analyze particular estimators or coarse graph quantities; a resolution must exploit typical random-regular geometry for the upper bound while retaining a converse against every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable, possibly biased or randomized estimator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit evaluable r(n,d) with every logarithmic factor fixed, universal c,C>0, a high-probability equivalence c r(n,d)≤R₂(G)≤C r(n,d), and a finite graph-dependent assignment sampler and observed-data estimator attaining the upper edge.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The new presolve reduces the dense-range fourth-trace calculation to the signed combination s−4pt+p²(4a+2b)−3p⁴. Bounding its five probabilities separately is insufficient because independent-witness and shared-witness contributions are individually much larger than d⁴/n³ and must cancel before coarse estimates are applied. Ordinary adjacency bounds control only the walk-count component, while fixed-shape graph-matrix results do not automatically handle Booleanization, direct edges among the four roots, shared witnesses, and residual-degree dependence uniformly near d=o(√n). The finite six- and eight-vertex enumerations validate identities but provide no asymptotic bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A four-root switching or joint no-hit expansion with a uniform signed remainder proving the displayed moment bound and hence the required operator/covariance estimate, or a quantified counterexample regime followed by evaluation of the weaker direct covariance certificate.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The archived least-favourable Beta–Bernoulli prior uses only the maximum balanced pair of simultaneously exposed treated and control endpoint sets, producing the logarithmic lower edge. A d²/n converse would need to aggregate information loss over many overlapping exposure conflicts rather than rely on one extremal balanced hole. Conversely, if a log-tuned seed or another design attains the smaller scale, then the packing prior may already capture the correct obstruction. Ordinary random-regular independence results do not settle the signed two-arm packing geometry, and fixed-estimator lower bounds cannot exclude nonlinear or biased procedures.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a graph-dependent least-favourable prior or testing inequality proving R₂(G)≥c d²/n, or a high-probability characterization of the balanced-exposure statistic together with an explicit procedure matching its induced d²/[n log(d+1)] or intermediate risk scale.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor exposure-menu construction obtains a finite saddle by reducing an L∞-bounded outcome model to sign schedules and observation fibres. That first reduction does not transfer verbatim: the present adversary is a pair of empirical-L2 endpoint balls, irrelevant exposures are unrestricted, and the estimator may be biased or nonlinear. The conflict graph identifies observational incompatibility but does not itself produce an evaluable exact game. New work needs an ellipsoidal extreme-point, least-favourable-prior, or complete-class argument before symmetry, orbit, fractional-cover, or covariance compression can be applied to the random-regular graph.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite primal-dual program or explicit functional F(G), recovery maps for a realizable assignment law and observed-data estimator, and universal constants c,C satisfying cF(G)≤R₂(G)≤CF(G), followed by a high-probability evaluation of F(G) as an explicit function of n and d.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The observed network defines a finite design problem -> conflict-graph invariance removes irrelevant outcome details -> coarse graph bounds leave the random-regular rate unresolved -> expose and evaluate the underlying finite saddle.

method_exemplars.technique: Begin from its conflict-graph quotient and design-adaptive Bayes lower bounds, then seek strong duality with an upper design problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact destination experiment and proves that the risk is a conflict-graph functional without evaluating that functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-based Riesz representers to express the best linear unbiased rule and its norm, then prove or refute a complete-class comparison with biased and nonlinear procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems concern linear causal functionals observed through design-dependent partial evaluations of fixed potential-outcome schedules.

literature_map:
Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) is the exact anchor: it defines unrestricted design-based minimax risk, reduces it to an exposure conflict graph, and leaves random-regular GATE between d/n and d²/n.
Kandiros–Pipis–Daskalakis–Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) gives Conflict Graph Design, a modified HT estimator, O(λ(H)/n) variance, and conservative inference; it is the closest constructive upper-bound method.
Ugander–Karrer–Backstrom–Kleinberg (KDD 2013, arXiv:1305.6979) introduced graph cluster randomization and exact exposure-probability computation.
Ugander–Yin (Journal of Causal Inference 2023, arXiv:2009.02297) randomizes the clustering itself and obtains polynomial exposure-variance bounds under metric-growth restrictions.
Karrer et al. (2020, arXiv:2012.08591) documents Facebook's deployed cluster-randomized GATE framework and motivates a degree-sensitive global-rollout precision benchmark.
Eckles–Karrer–Ugander (Journal of Causal Inference 2017, doi:10.1515/jci-2015-0021) studies the same all-treated versus all-control contrast and its design bias-variance tradeoff.
Viviano–Lei–Imbens et al. (arXiv:2310.14983) optimizes worst-case GATE MSE within a restricted cluster-design/difference-in-means class using min-cut and SDP machinery.
Aronow–Samii (Annals of Applied Statistics 2017, doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) supplies the exposure-mapping IPW framework, design-based variance bounds, and local-dependence asymptotics.
Harshaw–Middleton–Sävje (JASA 2026, arXiv:2112.01709) characterizes optimized conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference, but for a fixed design-estimator spine.
Basse–Airoldi (Sociological Methodology 2018, arXiv:1705.05752) shows that unbiasedness under interference need not imply concentration, supporting an unrestricted rather than HT-only minimax comparison.
Cook–Goldstein–Johnson (Annals of Probability 2018, arXiv:1510.06013) controls the nontrivial adjacency spectrum directly on the uniform simple regular law through d=O(n^(2/3)).
Bauerschmidt–Huang–Knowles–Yau (GAFA 2020, arXiv:1910.10121) gives sharper growing-degree adjacency spectral control, but not Boolean radius-two reachability.
Xu (CCC 2025, arXiv:2411.14314) supplies switching-based polynomial graph-matrix norm bounds; Booleanization and the signed four-root cancellation remain outside the stated result.
Abbe–Boix–Ralli–Sandon (SIAM Mathematics of Data Science 2020, arXiv:1809.04818) studies Boolean graph powering and spectral robustness, but its sparse-model radius conditions do not cover the dense regular subrange here.
Cooper–Frieze–Reed–Riordan (CPC 2002), Janson (RSA 2020), and McKay–Wormald–Wysocka (EJC 2004) provide independence, switching, and short-cycle tools; none evaluates the balanced two-arm minimax game or the required signed four-root moment.
